posts.title: “Asylum seekers stay in hotels for good”
posts.summary: A claim that's widely shared online. The figures say hotel use has halved in a year.

blocks.claim: Asylum seekers are put up in hotels and stay there for good.
blocks.speaker: Widely shared claim
blocks.summary: Hotel use is falling fast. 16,000 people were in asylum hotels in June 2026, half the number a year earlier, as faster decisions cut the backlog by 56%.

blocks.text: Hotels are the most expensive way to house people, at around £145 per person per night. Hotel costs fell from £8.3m a day in 2023/24 to £5.8m a day in 2024/25. The government has committed to ending hotel use within this Parliament.
Source: Home Office immigration system statistics (June 2026); Home Office Annual Report and Accounts
